forbidden.name: react
forbidden.why: A rule about what the product means cannot depend on how one surface draws it; a domain that imports React cannot be used by the CLI, the extension or a background job.

forbidden.name: tauri
forbidden.why: The desktop host is one place the domain runs, not a thing the domain knows about.

forbidden.name: expo
forbidden.why: The mobile host is one place the domain runs, not a thing the domain knows about.

forbidden.name: provider-sdk
forbidden.why: A provider is an implementation of the routing contract. A domain that imports one cannot be routed to another.

forbidden.name: stripe
forbidden.why: Billing is a provider behind the entitlement contract; the plans and the credits are the product's own.

forbidden.name: database-client
forbidden.why: Storage is an adapter. A domain that opens a connection cannot be evaluated on a client, in a test, or against another store.

forbidden.name: extension-api
forbidden.why: A browser extension API is one host's surface, and the domain has to run where it does not exist.

rootsWithoutDomain.why: The CLI is Rust. Its half of the contract is the generated protocol in crates/agiworkforce-protocol, which check-cross-version-matrix already holds to the TypeScript side.
The database adapter declares its own DatabaseAdapter interface rather than implementing a port the contracts own, so a second store would be a second interface.
rootsWithoutDomain.fix: Move the adapter interface into the contract package and have the adapter implement it.
